surfaces.part: rib arches (row of curved bones, flat face-on view)

answer.evidence: The ribs are drawn as a flat, face-on silhouette of arches. Each rib is a vertical band that curves up and over, with a dark outline on one side and a light fill. The rows at the top (10-16) are the arch curve itself, not a horizontal surface. No band ends in a front-edge line and none is followed by eave shadow. No ellipse is visible and no contents can be seen. The snow drift at rows 38-45 is a lumpy white mass with no edge line, so it adds no top surface. The bones and snow are scattered as debris, so the kind plausibly fits, but there is no top plane and the drawing reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of curved bone ribs on a snow base. It has about 11 visible tones per 16x16 tile, close to the hedge reference (9) and below the well (20) and cheese stall (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The ribs show roughly 4 bone steps (light cream, mid, a pinkish-grey shade, dark grey-brown), and the snow base has 2-3 blue-white steps. Both are below the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses per material. The dark edge pixels are 47% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: some pixels are tinted and others look grey. This is close to the neutral outline of the lamp and bench references, but it is not a uniform sticker line. The ribs are thin, uniform curved strokes with little per-bone grain, knobs or cracks, which makes them read flatter and thinner than the references. The snow bank is smooth, with few clumps or sparkle dots. It is decent, but a careful artist would likely see it as a step shallower than the reference props.

surfaces.part: rib arches (bone ribcage standing as arches)

answer.evidence: The ribs are drawn as a row of curved bone arches seen face-on in side elevation, spanning rows 7-40 with a snow drift at rows 38-45. The column scans show bone bands with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The widths grow smoothly (10:20, 14:49, 16:59), which is the arch silhouette and not a horizontal top plane. Dark outline pixels at rows 12-14 are bone shading and not an edge line. The drift at the bottom has a lighter top at rows 38-43, but it is a minor detail and does not read as a top surface for the main body. The arches show no horizontal surface, so the object reads as a front elevation. It does fit the debris kind loosely, as bones lying on the floor.
